import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Shelah's eventual categoricity conjecture

An *abstract elementary class* (AEC) is a class $K$ of structures in a fixed first-order
language $L$, closed under isomorphism, together with a partial order $\prec_K$ on $K$ refining
the substructure relation, satisfying the coherence axiom, the Tarski–Vaught chain axioms and a
Löwenheim–Skolem axiom. The least Löwenheim–Skolem cardinal is denoted $\mathrm{LS}(K)$.
$K$ is *categorical* in a cardinal $\kappa$ if it has exactly one model of cardinality $\kappa$
up to isomorphism.

Shelah's eventual categoricity conjecture asserts that there is a Hanf number for categoricity:
for every cardinal $\lambda$ there is a cardinal $\mu(\lambda)$ such that every AEC $K$ with
$\mathrm{LS}(K) \le \lambda$ that is categorical in some cardinal $\ge \mu(\lambda)$ is
categorical in every cardinal $\ge \mu(\lambda)$.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia: List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- [Wikipedia: Abstract elementary class](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abstract_elementary_class)
- [Sh394] S. Shelah, *Categoricity for abstract classes with amalgamation*,
  Annals of Pure and Applied Logic 98 (1999), 261–294. [arXiv:math/9809197](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/9809197)
- [Bon14] W. Boney, *Tameness from large cardinal axioms*, Journal of Symbolic Logic 79 (2014),
  1092–1119. [arXiv:1303.0550](https://arxiv.org/abs/1303.0550)
-/

namespace ShelahsEventualCategoricityConjecture

open Cardinal FirstOrder FirstOrder.Language

universe u v

/--
An abstract elementary class (AEC) in the language `L`.

The class `K` of models is given by the predicate `Mem` on `L`-structures (in the universe
`Type (max u v)`), and the strong substructure relation `≺_K` is given by `IsStrong`: for a
substructure `S` of an `L`-structure `M`, `IsStrong S` means `S ≺_K M`. Since `M ≺_K N` forces
`M` to be a substructure of `N`, this encodes the whole relation `≺_K`.

The axioms are the standard ones (Shelah [Sh394, Definition 0.A], Boney [Bon14, Definition 2.1],
Wikipedia): `≺_K` is a partial order on `K` refining the substructure relation; `K` and `≺_K`
are closed under isomorphisms; coherence; the Tarski–Vaught chain axioms; and the
Löwenheim–Skolem axiom, with `LS(K)` the least Löwenheim–Skolem cardinal `≥ |L| + ℵ₀`.

The union of a `≺_K`-chain is taken as a chain of substructures of an arbitrary ambient
`L`-structure `M` (which need not belong to `K`); every chain of structures can be realised
this way inside its union.
-/
structure AbstractElementaryClass (L : FirstOrder.Language.{u, v}) where
  /-- Membership in the class: `Mem M` means `M ∈ K`. -/
  Mem : ∀ (M : Type (max u v)) [L.Structure M], Prop
  /-- The strong substructure relation: `IsStrong S` means `S ≺_K M` for `S` a substructure
  of `M`. -/
  IsStrong : ∀ {M : Type (max u v)} [L.Structure M], L.Substructure M → Prop
  /-- `≺_K` is a relation on `K`: if `S ≺_K M` then `S ∈ K`. -/
  mem_left_of_isStrong : ∀ {M : Type (max u v)} [L.Structure M] (S : L.Substructure M),
    IsStrong S → Mem S
  /-- `≺_K` is a relation on `K`: if `S ≺_K M` then `M ∈ K`. -/
  mem_right_of_isStrong : ∀ {M : Type (max u v)} [L.Structure M] (S : L.Substructure M),
    IsStrong S → Mem M
  /-- Reflexivity: `M ≺_K M` for every `M ∈ K`. -/
  isStrong_top : ∀ (M : Type (max u v)) [L.Structure M],
    Mem M → IsStrong (⊤ : L.Substructure M)
  /-- Transitivity: if `T ≺_K S` and `S ≺_K M` then `T ≺_K M`. -/
  isStrong_trans : ∀ {M : Type (max u v)} [L.Structure M] (S : L.Substructure M)
    (T : L.Substructure S), IsStrong S → IsStrong T → IsStrong (T.map S.subtype.toHom)
  /-- `K` is closed under isomorphisms. -/
  mem_of_equiv : ∀ {M N : Type (max u v)} [L.Structure M] [L.Structure N],
    Mem M → (M ≃[L] N) → Mem N
  /-- `≺_K` is closed under isomorphisms: if `S ≺_K M` and `f : M ≃[L] N` then
  `f(S) ≺_K N`. -/
  isStrong_map_equiv : ∀ {M N : Type (max u v)} [L.Structure M] [L.Structure N]
    (f : M ≃[L] N) (S : L.Substructure M), IsStrong S → IsStrong (S.map f.toHom)
  /-- Coherence: if `S ≺_K M`, `T ≺_K M` and `S ⊆ T`, then `S ≺_K T`. -/
  isStrong_comap_of_le : ∀ {M : Type (max u v)} [L.Structure M] {S T : L.Substructure M},
    IsStrong S → IsStrong T → S ≤ T → IsStrong (S.comap T.subtype.toHom)
  /-- Tarski–Vaught chain axiom (unions): if `(S i)` is a nonempty well-ordered `≺_K`-chain of
  models in `K`, then its union `⨆ i, S i` is in `K` and `S i ≺_K ⨆ j, S j` for every `i`. -/
  mem_iSup_of_chain : ∀ {M : Type (max u v)} [L.Structure M] {ι : Type (max u v)}
    [LinearOrder ι] [WellFoundedLT ι] [Nonempty ι] (S : ι → L.Substructure M),
    (∀ i, Mem (S i)) →
    (∀ i j, i < j → S i ≤ S j ∧ IsStrong ((S i).comap (S j).subtype.toHom)) →
    Mem ↥(⨆ i, S i) ∧ ∀ i, IsStrong ((S i).comap (⨆ j, S j).subtype.toHom)
  /-- Tarski–Vaught chain axiom (smoothness): if `(S i)` is a nonempty well-ordered `≺_K`-chain
  with `S i ≺_K N` for every `i`, then `⨆ i, S i ≺_K N`. -/
  isStrong_iSup_of_chain : ∀ {N : Type (max u v)} [L.Structure N] {ι : Type (max u v)}
    [LinearOrder ι] [WellFoundedLT ι] [Nonempty ι] (S : ι → L.Substructure N),
    (∀ i j, i < j → S i ≤ S j ∧ IsStrong ((S i).comap (S j).subtype.toHom)) →
    (∀ i, IsStrong (S i)) → IsStrong (⨆ i, S i)
  /-- The Löwenheim–Skolem number `LS(K)`. -/
  lsNumber : Cardinal.{max u v}
  /-- Löwenheim–Skolem axiom: `LS(K)` is the least cardinal `μ ≥ |L| + ℵ₀` such that every
  subset `A` of a model `M ∈ K` is contained in some `S ≺_K M` with `‖S‖ ≤ |A| + μ`. -/
  lsNumber_isLeast : IsLeast {μ : Cardinal.{max u v} | L.card + ℵ₀ ≤ μ ∧
    ∀ (M : Type (max u v)) [L.Structure M], Mem M → ∀ A : Set M,
      ∃ S : L.Substructure M, A ⊆ S ∧ IsStrong S ∧ #S ≤ #A + μ} lsNumber

namespace AbstractElementaryClass

variable {L : FirstOrder.Language.{u, v}}

/-- An AEC `K` is *categorical* in the cardinal `κ` if it has exactly one model of
cardinality `κ` up to isomorphism. -/
def IsCategoricalIn (K : AbstractElementaryClass L) (κ : Cardinal.{max u v}) : Prop :=
  (∃ (M : Type (max u v)) (_ : L.Structure M), K.Mem M ∧ #M = κ) ∧
    ∀ (M N : Type (max u v)) [L.Structure M] [L.Structure N],
      K.Mem M → K.Mem N → #M = κ → #N = κ → Nonempty (M ≃[L] N)

open FirstOrder.Language.Substructure in
/-- The class of all `L`-structures, with `≺_K` the substructure relation, is an AEC with
Löwenheim–Skolem number `|L| + ℵ₀`. -/
def univ (L : FirstOrder.Language.{u, v}) : AbstractElementaryClass L where
  Mem _ := True
  IsStrong _ := True
  mem_left_of_isStrong _ _ := trivial
  mem_right_of_isStrong _ _ := trivial
  isStrong_top _ _ _ := trivial
  isStrong_trans _ _ _ _ := trivial
  mem_of_equiv _ _ := trivial
  isStrong_map_equiv _ _ _ := trivial
  isStrong_comap_of_le _ _ _ := trivial
  mem_iSup_of_chain _ _ _ := ⟨trivial, fun _ => trivial⟩
  isStrong_iSup_of_chain _ _ _ := trivial
  lsNumber := L.card + ℵ₀
  lsNumber_isLeast := by
    refine ⟨⟨le_rfl, fun M _ _ A => ⟨closure L A, subset_closure, trivial, ?_⟩⟩,
      fun μ hμ => hμ.1⟩
    have h := lift_card_closure_le (L := L) (s := A)
    rw [lift_id', lift_id'] at h
    have hf : lift.{max u v, u} #(Σ i, L.Functions i) ≤ L.card := by
      rw [card, mk_sum, lift_umax.{u, v}]
      exact le_self_add
    exact h.trans (max_le (le_add_left le_add_self) (add_le_add le_rfl (hf.trans le_self_add)))

/-- In the empty language, the class of all structures is categorical in every cardinal. -/
@[category test, AMS 3]
theorem univ_empty_isCategoricalIn (κ : Cardinal) :
    (univ FirstOrder.Language.empty).IsCategoricalIn κ := by
  refine ⟨⟨κ.out, FirstOrder.Language.emptyStructure, trivial, mk_out κ⟩,
    fun M N _ _ _ _ hM hN => ?_⟩
  rw [empty.nonempty_equiv_iff, lift_id, lift_id, hM, hN]

end AbstractElementaryClass

/--
**Shelah's eventual categoricity conjecture.**
For every cardinal $\lambda$ there exists a cardinal $\mu(\lambda)$ such that if an AEC $K$ with
$\mathrm{LS}(K) \le \lambda$ is categorical in some cardinal $\nu \ge \mu(\lambda)$, then it is
categorical in every cardinal $\theta \ge \mu(\lambda)$.

The cardinal $\mu(\lambda)$ depends only on $\lambda$, not on $K$ (nor on its language).
Following Shelah and Boney, "above $\mu(\lambda)$" is read as $\ge \mu(\lambda)$. In the Lean
statement, `κ` plays the role of $\lambda$.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 3]
theorem shelahs_eventual_categoricity_conjecture (κ : Cardinal.{max u v}) :
    ∃ μ : Cardinal.{max u v}, ∀ (L : FirstOrder.Language.{u, v})
      (K : AbstractElementaryClass L), K.lsNumber ≤ κ →
        (∃ ν, μ ≤ ν ∧ K.IsCategoricalIn ν) → ∀ θ, μ ≤ θ → K.IsCategoricalIn θ := by
  sorry

end ShelahsEventualCategoricityConjecture
attempts.decomposition_objections: None. The single-slot decomposition and its notes (∀λ ∃μ ∀K order; categoricity as exactly one model up to isomorphism; ≥ reading of 'above'; LS(K) ≤ λ; LS axiom with LS(K) ≥ |L(K)| + ℵ₀; exclusion of the stronger Hanf-number conjectures) were followed. One remark: the Wikipedia definition of AEC omits the standard chain clause M_α ≺_K ⋃ M_β (present in Shelah and Boney); the formalization includes it, since the conjecture concerns AECs in Shelah's sense.
modeling_decisions: Quantifier order is ∀λ ∃μ ∀L ∀K: μ depends only on λ, not on the AEC K or its language L. The theorem takes λ as the explicit argument `κ` (since `λ` cannot be used as a Lean identifier) and existentially quantifies μ.

'Above μ(λ)' is read as ≥ μ(λ) (non-strict) in both the hypothesis and the conclusion, following Boney's statement of D.(3a) and the Wikipedia article; the hypothesis is `∃ ν, μ ≤ ν ∧ K.IsCategoricalIn ν` (conjunction, not implication).
`IsCategoricalIn K κ` means exactly one model of cardinality κ up to isomorphism: existence of a model in K of cardinality κ AND any two such models are L-isomorphic (`Nonempty (M ≃[L] N)`).

AEC encoding: the class is a predicate `Mem` on L-structures with carrier in `Type (max u v)` for `L : Language.{u, v}` (so language and models live in one cardinal universe `Cardinal.{max u v}`; any language fits, models in smaller universes can be lifted). The relation ≺_K is encoded as a predicate `IsStrong` on substructures: `IsStrong S` means `S ≺_K M` for `S : L.Substructure M`. Since `M ≺_K N` forces M to be a substructure of N, this captures the whole relation; `M ≺_K N` for abstract structures is recovered via isomorphism-closure.

Axioms included (following Shelah [Sh394, Def. 0.A], Boney [Bon14, Def. 2.1], Wikipedia): ≺_K is a relation on K (both sides in K), reflexive (`⊤ ≺_K M` for M ∈ K) and transitive; K and ≺_K are closed under L-isomorphisms; coherence; Tarski–Vaught chain axioms; Löwenheim–Skolem axiom with LS(K) ≥ |L| + ℵ₀. Antisymmetry is automatic in the substructure encoding.

Chain axioms are stated for nonempty well-ordered (`LinearOrder ι`, `WellFoundedLT ι`, `Nonempty ι`) chains of substructures `S i` of an arbitrary ambient L-structure (not required to be in K) with `S i ≤ S j` and `S i ≺_K S j` for i < j; the union is `⨆ i, S i` (equal to the set-theoretic union for a chain). Every set-theoretic chain of structures lives inside its union, so this is equivalent to the usual formulation; well-ordered rather than arbitrary/continuous chains matches Wikipedia's 'γ an ordinal'. Besides Wikipedia's two conclusions (union in K; smoothness `⋃ M_α ≺_K N`), the standard clause `M_α ≺_K ⋃ M_β` (Shelah AxIII, Boney 6(a)), which Wikipedia omits, is included. The chain hypothesis also requires each `S i ∈ K`, needed for one-element chains.

The Löwenheim–Skolem number is a field `lsNumber` with axiom `lsNumber_isLeast : IsLeast {μ | L.card + ℵ₀ ≤ μ ∧ ∀ M ∈ K, ∀ A ⊆ M, ∃ S ≺_K M, A ⊆ S ∧ #S ≤ #A + μ} lsNumber`, i.e. LS(K) is the least Löwenheim–Skolem cardinal ≥ |L(K)| + ℵ₀, as in the Wikipedia definition; the data field is determined uniquely by the axiom.

The convention of discarding models of size < LS(K) is not imposed; it is immaterial for the conjecture (all cardinals involved are ≥ μ(λ)). The article's stronger conjectures (Hanf number of PC classes; ℶ_{ω₁} for L_{ω₁,ω}) are not formalized, per the decomposition table.

Sanity checks added: `AbstractElementaryClass.univ L` (all L-structures with the substructure relation) is an AEC with LS number |L| + ℵ₀, and a `category test` theorem that `univ Language.empty` is categorical in every cardinal, showing the structure and `IsCategoricalIn` are satisfiable and non-vacuous.

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Shelah's eventual categoricity conjecture

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, Abstract elementary class](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abstract_elementary_class)
- [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- W. Boney, [Tameness from large cardinal axioms](https://arxiv.org/abs/1303.0550)
-/

namespace ShelahsEventualCategoricityConjecture

open Cardinal FirstOrder FirstOrder.Language

universe u

/-- A cardinal has the Löwenheim–Skolem hull property for a class of structures with a
specified notion of strong embedding. -/
def HasLSProperty (L : FirstOrder.Language.{u, u})
    (Model : ∀ M : Type u, L.Structure M → Prop)
    (StrongEmbedding : ∀ {M N : Type u} [L.Structure M] [L.Structure N],
      (M ↪[L] N) → Prop) (κ : Cardinal.{u}) : Prop :=
  L.card + ℵ₀ ≤ κ ∧
    ∀ (M : Type u) [L.Structure M], Model M inferInstance → ∀ A : Set M,
      ∃ (N : Type u) (_ : L.Structure N) (f : N ↪[L] M),
        StrongEmbedding f ∧ (∀ a ∈ A, a ∈ Set.range f) ∧ #N ≤ #A + κ

/-- An abstract elementary class, presented by its models and strong embeddings.
The axioms are the isomorphism, coherence, directed-union, and Löwenheim–Skolem
axioms in their embedding-based form. -/
structure AbstractElementaryClass where
  Language : FirstOrder.Language.{u, u}
  Model : ∀ M : Type u, Language.Structure M → Prop
  StrongEmbedding : ∀ {M N : Type u} [Language.Structure M] [Language.Structure N],
    (M ↪[Language] N) → Prop
  model_nonempty : ∀ (M : Type u) [Language.Structure M], Model M inferInstance → Nonempty M
  strong_models : ∀ {M N : Type u} [Language.Structure M] [Language.Structure N]
    (f : M ↪[Language] N), StrongEmbedding f → Model M inferInstance ∧ Model N inferInstance
  model_of_equiv : ∀ {M N : Type u} [Language.Structure M] [Language.Structure N],
    Model M inferInstance → (M ≃[Language] N) → Model N inferInstance
  equiv_strong : ∀ {M N : Type u} [Language.Structure M] [Language.Structure N]
    (e : M ≃[Language] N), Model M inferInstance → StrongEmbedding e.toEmbedding
  strong_id : ∀ (M : Type u) [Language.Structure M], Model M inferInstance →
    StrongEmbedding (Embedding.refl Language M)
  strong_comp : ∀ {M N P : Type u} [Language.Structure M] [Language.Structure N]
    [Language.Structure P] (f : M ↪[Language] N) (g : N ↪[Language] P),
    StrongEmbedding f → StrongEmbedding g → StrongEmbedding (g.comp f)
  coherence : ∀ {M N P : Type u} [Language.Structure M] [Language.Structure N]
    [Language.Structure P] (f : M ↪[Language] N) (g : N ↪[Language] P),
    StrongEmbedding g → StrongEmbedding (g.comp f) → StrongEmbedding f
  directed_limits : ∀ (ι : Type u) [Preorder ι] [IsDirectedOrder ι] [Nonempty ι]
    (G : ι → Type u) [∀ i, Language.Structure (G i)]
    (f : ∀ i j, i ≤ j → G i ↪[Language] G j)
    [DirectedSystem G fun i j h => f i j h],
    (∀ i, Model (G i) inferInstance) →
    (∀ i j (h : i ≤ j), StrongEmbedding (f i j h)) →
    Model (FirstOrder.Language.DirectLimit G f) inferInstance ∧
      (∀ i, StrongEmbedding (FirstOrder.Language.DirectLimit.of Language ι G f i)) ∧
      ∀ (N : Type u) [Language.Structure N] (g : ∀ i, G i ↪[Language] N),
        (∀ i, StrongEmbedding (g i)) →
        (hcomm : ∀ i j hij x, g j (f i j hij x) = g i x) →
        StrongEmbedding (FirstOrder.Language.DirectLimit.lift Language ι G f g hcomm)
  lsNumber : Cardinal.{u}
  lsNumber_property : HasLSProperty Language Model StrongEmbedding lsNumber
  lsNumber_le : ∀ κ, HasLSProperty Language Model StrongEmbedding κ → lsNumber ≤ κ

namespace AbstractElementaryClass

/-- An AEC is categorical in `κ` when it has a model of cardinality `κ` and any
two such models are isomorphic. -/
def Categorical
    (K : ShelahsEventualCategoricityConjecture.AbstractElementaryClass)
    (κ : Cardinal.{u}) : Prop :=
  (∃ (M : Type u) (_ : K.Language.Structure M),
      K.Model M inferInstance ∧ #M = κ) ∧
    ∀ (M N : Type u) [K.Language.Structure M] [K.Language.Structure N],
      K.Model M inferInstance → K.Model N inferInstance →
      #M = κ → #N = κ → Nonempty (M ≃[K.Language] N)

end AbstractElementaryClass

/--
**Shelah's eventual categoricity conjecture.** For every cardinal $\lambda$ there is a
cardinal $\mu(\lambda)$ such that, for every abstract elementary class $K$ with
$\operatorname{LS}(K) \leq \lambda$, if $K$ is categorical in some cardinal
$\kappa \geq \mu(\lambda)$, then it is categorical in every cardinal
$\theta \geq \mu(\lambda)$. Here categorical means having exactly one model of that
cardinality up to isomorphism.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 03]
theorem shelahs_eventual_categoricity_conjecture :
    ∀ (lam : Cardinal.{u}), ∃ (mu : Cardinal.{u}),
      ∀ K : ShelahsEventualCategoricityConjecture.AbstractElementaryClass,
      K.lsNumber ≤ lam →
      (∃ κ ≥ mu, K.Categorical κ) →
      ∀ θ ≥ mu, K.Categorical θ := by
  sorry

end ShelahsEventualCategoricityConjecture
modeling_decisions: Read “above μ(λ)” as greater than or equal to μ(λ), following both the background article and Boney’s formulation.
Kept the source’s quantifier order `∀ λ, ∃ μ, ∀ K`, so the threshold depends only on λ and not on the AEC.
Used the list statement’s hypothesis `LS(K) ≤ λ` rather than Boney’s `LS(K) = λ`.

Defined categoricity to include existence of a model of the specified cardinality as well as uniqueness up to first-order-language isomorphism, matching the article’s phrase “exactly one (up to isomorphism) model.”

Presented an AEC as a universe-polymorphic class predicate over all structures, together with strong embeddings, rather than as a small type of models; this avoids imposing an unintended bound on model cardinalities.

Encoded the partial-order, isomorphism, coherence, and Tarski–Vaught chain axioms in the standard equivalent strong-embedding/direct-limit form. Nonempty directed systems correspond to the nonempty chain convention for AEC unions.
Defined `LS(K)` as the least cardinal at least `|L(K)| + ℵ₀` satisfying the downward strong-submodel hull property.

Used a single Lean universe for the language symbols, model carriers, and cardinals. The declaration is universe-polymorphic, so this is the usual universe-bounded representation rather than a restriction to any fixed mathematical cardinal.

    {M₀ : L.Substructure M}, StrongSubstructure N M → StrongSubstructure (bundledSubstructure M) M₀ →
      StrongSubstructure N (M₀.map M.subtype.toHom)
  /-- Coherence of strong substructure. -/
  coherence : ∀ {N : BundledStructure L} {M₀ M₁ : L.Substructure N},
    StrongSubstructure N M₀ → StrongSubstructure N M₁ → M₀ ≤ M₁ →
      StrongSubstructure (bundledSubstructure M₁) (M₀.comap M₁.subtype.toHom)
  /-- Unions of nonempty increasing chains are models and contain every stage strongly. -/
  chain_union : ∀ {ι : Type u} [LinearOrder ι] [Nonempty ι] {N : BundledStructure L}
    (M : ι → L.Substructure N),
    (∀ i, bundledSubstructure (M i) ∈ models) →
    (∀ i j, i ≤ j → M i ≤ M j ∧
      StrongSubstructure (bundledSubstructure (M j)) ((M i).comap (M j).subtype.toHom)) →
    let U := sSup (Set.range M)
    bundledSubstructure U ∈ models ∧ ∀ i, StrongSubstructure (bundledSubstructure U) ((M i).comap U.subtype.toHom)
  /-- The union of a strong chain inside a model is strong in that model. -/
  chain_union_strong : ∀ {ι : Type u} [LinearOrder ι] [Nonempty ι]
    {N : BundledStructure L} (M : ι → L.Substructure N),
    (∀ i j, i ≤ j → M i ≤ M j) → (∀ i, StrongSubstructure N (M i)) →
      StrongSubstructure N (sSup (Set.range M))
  /-- The Löwenheim--Skolem number of the class. -/
  lsNumber : Cardinal.{u}
  /-- `lsNumber` is the least cardinal satisfying the Löwenheim--Skolem axiom. -/
  lsNumber_isLeast : IsLeast
    {μ : Cardinal.{u} | L.card + ℵ₀ ≤ μ ∧
      ∀ (N : BundledStructure L), N ∈ models → ∀ A : Set N,
        ∃ M : L.Substructure N, StrongSubstructure N M ∧
          A ⊆ M ∧ #M ≤ #A + μ}
    lsNumber

namespace AbstractElementaryClass

/-- An AEC is categorical in `κ` when it has a model of size `κ` and any two such models are
isomorphic. -/
def Categorical {L : FirstOrder.Language.{u, u}} (K : AbstractElementaryClass L)
    (κ : Cardinal.{u}) : Prop :=
  (∃ M : BundledStructure L, M ∈ K.models ∧ #M = κ) ∧
    ∀ M N : BundledStructure L, M ∈ K.models → N ∈ K.models →
      #M = κ → #N = κ → Nonempty (M ≃[L] N)

end AbstractElementaryClass

/--

$\mu(\lambda)$ such that, for every abstract elementary class $K$ with
$\operatorname{LS}(K) \leq \lambda$, if $K$ is categorical in some cardinal at least
$\mu(\lambda)$, then it is categorical in every cardinal at least $\mu(\lambda)$.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 3]
theorem shelahs_eventual_categoricity_conjecture :
    ∀ lam : Cardinal.{u}, ∃ mu : Cardinal.{u}, ∀ (L : FirstOrder.Language.{u, u})
      (K : AbstractElementaryClass L), K.lsNumber ≤ lam →
      (∃ kappa : Cardinal.{u}, mu ≤ kappa ∧ K.Categorical kappa) →
      ∀ theta : Cardinal.{u}, mu ≤ theta → K.Categorical theta := by
  sorry

end ShelahsEventualCategoricityConjecture

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Shelah's eventual categoricity conjecture

An *abstract elementary class* (AEC) is a class $K$ of structures in a first-order language
$L = L(K)$ together with a partial order $\prec_K$ ("strong substructure") on $K$, refining the
substructure relation, closed under isomorphisms, satisfying coherence, the Tarski–Vaught chain
axioms and a Löwenheim–Skolem axiom. The *Löwenheim–Skolem number* $\operatorname{LS}(K)$ is the
least cardinal $\mu \ge |L(K)| + \aleph_0$ such that every subset $A$ of a model $M \in K$ is
contained in some $N \prec_K M$ with $\|N\| \le |A| + \mu$.

$K$ is *categorical* in a cardinal $\kappa$ if it has exactly one model of cardinality $\kappa$
up to isomorphism.

Shelah's eventual categoricity conjecture: for every cardinal $\lambda$ there exists a cardinal
$\mu(\lambda)$ such that if an AEC $K$ with $\operatorname{LS}(K) \le \lambda$ is categorical in a
cardinal $\ge \mu(\lambda)$, then it is categorical in all cardinals $\ge \mu(\lambda)$.

Since Mathlib has no notion of abstract elementary class, this file defines one. Strong
substructures are encoded by a class of `L`-embeddings, the `K`-embeddings: an `L`-embedding
`f : M ↪[L] N` is a `K`-embedding exactly when `f[M] ≺_K N`. Unions of chains are encoded by
`FirstOrder.Language.DirectLimit`.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- [Wikipedia, Abstract elementary class](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abstract_elementary_class)
- [S. Shelah, *Categoricity for abstract classes with amalgamation*](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/9809197)
- [W. Boney, *Tameness from large cardinal axioms*](https://arxiv.org/abs/1303.0550)
-/

namespace ShelahsEventualCategoricityConjecture

open FirstOrder FirstOrder.Language Cardinal

universe u

variable (L : FirstOrder.Language.{u, u})

/-- The data underlying an abstract elementary class: a class `K` of `L`-structures (with
universes in `Type u`) together with a class of `L`-embeddings between them, the `K`-embeddings.
An `L`-embedding `f : M ↪[L] N` is a `K`-embedding exactly when `f[M] ≺_K N`, where `≺_K` is the
strong substructure relation of `K`. In particular, for a substructure `N ≤ M`, `N ≺_K M` means
that the inclusion `N.subtype` is a `K`-embedding. -/
structure AbstractClass where
  /-- `IsModel M` means that the `L`-structure `M` belongs to the class `K`. -/
  IsModel : ∀ (M : Type u) [L.Structure M], Prop
  /-- `IsStrong f` means that the `L`-embedding `f : M ↪[L] N` is a `K`-embedding, i.e.
  `f[M] ≺_K N`. -/
  IsStrong : ∀ {M N : Type u} [L.Structure M] [L.Structure N], (M ↪[L] N) → Prop

variable {L}

namespace AbstractClass

/-- `K.IsLowenheimSkolemBound μ` means that `μ ≥ |L(K)| + ℵ₀` and that every subset `A` of a
model `M ∈ K` is contained in some `N ≺_K M` with `‖N‖ ≤ |A| + μ`. -/
def IsLowenheimSkolemBound (K : AbstractClass L) (μ : Cardinal.{u}) : Prop :=
  L.card + ℵ₀ ≤ μ ∧ ∀ (M : Type u) [L.Structure M], K.IsModel M → ∀ A : Set M,
    ∃ N : L.Substructure M, A ⊆ N ∧ #N ≤ #A + μ ∧ K.IsStrong N.subtype

/-- The Löwenheim–Skolem number `LS(K)` of `K`: the least cardinal `μ ≥ |L(K)| + ℵ₀` such that
every subset `A` of a model `M ∈ K` is contained in some `N ≺_K M` with `‖N‖ ≤ |A| + μ`. -/
noncomputable def lowenheimSkolemNumber (K : AbstractClass L) : Cardinal.{u} :=
  sInf {μ | K.IsLowenheimSkolemBound μ}

/-- `K.Categorical κ` means that `K` has exactly one model of cardinality `κ` up to
isomorphism. -/
def Categorical (K : AbstractClass L) (κ : Cardinal.{u}) : Prop :=
  (∃ (M : Type u) (_ : L.Structure M), K.IsModel M ∧ #M = κ) ∧
    ∀ (M N : Type u) [L.Structure M] [L.Structure N],
      K.IsModel M → K.IsModel N → #M = κ → #N = κ → Nonempty (M ≃[L] N)

end AbstractClass

variable (L) in
/-- An *abstract elementary class* (AEC) in the language `L`, with models in `Type u`.

It is given by a class `K` of `L`-structures together with the strong substructure relation
`≺_K`, encoded by the class of `K`-embeddings (`IsStrong`), subject to the following axioms.
* `≺_K` is a relation on `K`: a `K`-embedding goes between members of `K`.
* Isomorphisms: every isomorphism out of a member of `K` is a `K`-embedding (in particular `K` is
  closed under isomorphism and `≺_K` is reflexive on `K`), and `K`-embeddings are closed under
  composition (`≺_K` is transitive and respects isomorphisms).
* Coherence: if `M₁ ⊆ M₂ ≺_K M₃` and `M₁ ≺_K M₃`, then `M₁ ≺_K M₂`.
* Tarski–Vaught chain axioms: if `(Mᵢ)ᵢ` is a `≺_K`-chain indexed by a nonempty well-ordered
  type, then its union `⋃ᵢ Mᵢ` (the direct limit) is in `K`, `Mᵢ ≺_K ⋃ᵢ Mᵢ` for every `i`, and
  `⋃ᵢ Mᵢ ≺_K N` whenever `Mᵢ ≺_K N` for every `i`.
* Löwenheim–Skolem axiom: there is a cardinal `μ ≥ |L(K)| + ℵ₀` such that every subset `A` of a
  model `M ∈ K` is contained in some `N ≺_K M` with `‖N‖ ≤ |A| + μ`. -/
structure AbstractElementaryClass extends AbstractClass L where
  /-- `≺_K` is a relation on `K`. -/
  isModel_of_isStrong {M N : Type u} [L.Structure M] [L.Structure N] {f : M ↪[L] N} :
    IsStrong f → IsModel M ∧ IsModel N
  /-- Every isomorphism out of a member of `K` is a `K`-embedding. -/
  isStrong_equiv {M N : Type u} [L.Structure M] [L.Structure N] :
    IsModel M → ∀ e : M ≃[L] N, IsStrong e.toEmbedding
  /-- `K`-embeddings are closed under composition. -/
  isStrong_comp {M N P : Type u} [L.Structure M] [L.Structure N] [L.Structure P]
    {f : M ↪[L] N} {g : N ↪[L] P} : IsStrong f → IsStrong g → IsStrong (g.comp f)
  /-- Coherence: if `g` and `g ∘ f` are `K`-embeddings, then so is `f`. -/
  isStrong_of_comp {M N P : Type u} [L.Structure M] [L.Structure N] [L.Structure P]
    {f : M ↪[L] N} {g : N ↪[L] P} : IsStrong g → IsStrong (g.comp f) → IsStrong f
  /-- Chain axiom: the union of a `≺_K`-chain is in `K`. -/
  isModel_directLimit {ι : Type u} [LinearOrder ι] [WellFoundedLT ι] [Nonempty ι]
    {G : ι → Type u} [∀ i, L.Structure (G i)] (f : ∀ i j, i ≤ j → G i ↪[L] G j)
    [DirectedSystem G fun i j h => f i j h] :
    (∀ i j h, IsStrong (f i j h)) → IsModel (Language.DirectLimit G f)
  /-- Chain axiom: every member of a `≺_K`-chain is a strong substructure of the union. -/
  isStrong_directLimit_of {ι : Type u} [LinearOrder ι] [WellFoundedLT ι] [Nonempty ι]
    {G : ι → Type u} [∀ i, L.Structure (G i)] (f : ∀ i j, i ≤ j → G i ↪[L] G j)
    [DirectedSystem G fun i j h => f i j h] :
    (∀ i j h, IsStrong (f i j h)) → ∀ i, IsStrong (Language.DirectLimit.of L ι G f i)
  /-- Chain axiom: if every member of a `≺_K`-chain is a strong substructure of `N`, then so is
  the union. -/
  isStrong_directLimit_lift {ι : Type u} [LinearOrder ι] [WellFoundedLT ι] [Nonempty ι]
    {G : ι → Type u} [∀ i, L.Structure (G i)] (f : ∀ i j, i ≤ j → G i ↪[L] G j)
    [DirectedSystem G fun i j h => f i j h] {N : Type u} [L.Structure N]
    (g : ∀ i, G i ↪[L] N) (Hg : ∀ i j hij x, g j (f i j hij x) = g i x) :
    (∀ i j h, IsStrong (f i j h)) → (∀ i, IsStrong (g i)) →
      IsStrong (Language.DirectLimit.lift L ι G f g Hg)
  /-- Löwenheim–Skolem axiom. -/
  exists_isLowenheimSkolemBound : ∃ μ, toAbstractClass.IsLowenheimSkolemBound μ

namespace AbstractElementaryClass

variable (K : AbstractElementaryClass L) {M N : Type u} [L.Structure M] [L.Structure N]

/-- `K` is closed under isomorphism. -/
@[category API, AMS 3]
theorem isModel_of_equiv (hM : K.IsModel M) (e : M ≃[L] N) : K.IsModel N :=
  (K.isModel_of_isStrong (K.isStrong_equiv hM e)).2

/-- `≺_K` is reflexive on `K`. -/
@[category API, AMS 3]
theorem isStrong_refl (hM : K.IsModel M) : K.IsStrong (Embedding.refl L M) :=
  Language.Equiv.refl_toEmbedding (L := L) (M := M) ▸
    K.isStrong_equiv hM (Language.Equiv.refl L M)

variable (L) in
/-- The class of all `L`-structures, with all `L`-embeddings as `K`-embeddings, is an abstract
elementary class (with Löwenheim–Skolem number at most `|L| + ℵ₀`). -/
@[category test, AMS 3]
def univ : AbstractElementaryClass L where
  IsModel _ := True
  IsStrong _ := True
  isModel_of_isStrong _ := ⟨trivial, trivial⟩
  isStrong_equiv _ _ := trivial
  isStrong_comp _ _ := trivial
  isStrong_of_comp _ _ := trivial
  isModel_directLimit _ _ _ := trivial
  isStrong_directLimit_of _ _ _ _ := trivial
  isStrong_directLimit_lift _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ := trivial
  exists_isLowenheimSkolemBound := by
    refine ⟨L.card + ℵ₀, le_rfl, fun M _ _ A => ⟨Substructure.closure L A,
      Substructure.subset_closure, ?_, trivial⟩⟩
    have h := Substructure.lift_card_closure_le (L := L) (s := A)
    simp only [lift_id] at h
    have hF : #(Σ i, L.Functions i) ≤ L.card := by
      rw [card, mk_sum, lift_id, lift_id]
      exact le_self_add
    refine h.trans (max_le ?_ ?_)
    · exact le_add_left le_add_self
    · exact add_le_add_right (hF.trans le_self_add) _

end AbstractElementaryClass

/-- **Shelah's eventual categoricity conjecture.**
For every cardinal $\lambda$ there exists a cardinal $\mu(\lambda)$ such that if an abstract
elementary class $K$ with $\operatorname{LS}(K) \le \lambda$ is categorical in some cardinal
$\kappa \ge \mu(\lambda)$, then it is categorical in every cardinal $\kappa \ge \mu(\lambda)$.

Here $\mu(\lambda)$ depends only on $\lambda$, not on $K$, and "categorical in $\kappa$" means
that $K$ has exactly one model of cardinality $\kappa$ up to isomorphism. -/
@[category research open, AMS 3]
theorem shelahs_eventual_categoricity_conjecture :
    ∀ lam : Cardinal.{u}, ∃ μ : Cardinal.{u},
      ∀ (L : FirstOrder.Language.{u, u}) (K : AbstractElementaryClass L),
        K.lowenheimSkolemNumber ≤ lam → (∃ κ, μ ≤ κ ∧ K.Categorical κ) →
          ∀ κ, μ ≤ κ → K.Categorical κ := by
  sorry

end ShelahsEventualCategoricityConjecture

modeling_decisions: Encoding of ≺_K: instead of a relation on literal substructures (impossible across distinct Lean types), the AEC carries a class of L-embeddings (K-embeddings), with `IsStrong f` meaning f[M] ≺_K N; for a substructure N ≤ M, N ≺_K M is `IsStrong N.subtype`. This is the standard 'K-embedding'/categorical presentation of AECs and is equivalent to the set-theoretic one by the isomorphism axiom.

Isomorphism axiom stated as 'every isomorphism out of a member of K is a K-embedding' plus closure under composition; K's closure under isomorphism and reflexivity of ≺_K are derived (API lemmas `isModel_of_equiv`, `isStrong_refl`). Antisymmetry of ≺_K is automatic in the set-theoretic version and has no content in the embedding version.

Chain axioms use `FirstOrder.Language.DirectLimit` for the union of a chain, indexed by an arbitrary nonempty well-ordered type ι : Type u (equivalent to indexing by a nonzero ordinal γ); the chain hypothesis `∀ i j h, IsStrong (f i j h)` includes i = j, which just says each Mᵢ ∈ K. The clause Mᵢ ≺_K ⋃ Mⱼ is included (present in Shelah's AxIII, Boney's and Baldwin's definitions, omitted in the Wikipedia article's list) since the conjecture is about AECs in the standard sense.

Löwenheim–Skolem: LS(K) = sInf {μ | μ ≥ |L| + ℵ₀ ∧ every A ⊆ M ∈ K lies in some N ≺_K M with #N ≤ #A + μ}, following Wikipedia/Boney; the AEC axiom guarantees the set is nonempty, and it is upward closed, so `LS(K) ≤ λ` is equivalent to λ being a bound. Shelah's own variant (LS'(K) + |τ|) is not used.

Universes: all models, index types and the language live in `Type u` (`L : FirstOrder.Language.{u, u}`), and all cardinals are `Cardinal.{u}`; the theorem is universe-polymorphic. Since |L| ≤ LS(K) ≤ λ, restricting the language to universe u loses no generality.
'Above μ(λ)' read as ≥ μ(λ) in both hypothesis and conclusion, following Boney/Shelah D.(3a) and the article (equivalent up to adjusting μ). 'LS(K) ≤ λ' kept as in the statement (vs Boney's '= λ').
The Wikipedia article's convention of discarding models of size < LS(K) is not imposed; it is immaterial for categoricity above μ(λ).

For finite λ the hypothesis LS(K) ≤ λ is unsatisfiable (LS(K) ≥ ℵ₀), so those instances are vacuous, exactly as in the informal statement. The empty class is an AEC but never categorical; the class of all L-structures is an AEC (`univ` test).

/-!
# Shelah's eventual categoricity conjecture

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, Abstract elementary class](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abstract_elementary_class)
- [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics#Model_theory_and_formal_languages)
- S. Shelah, *Categoricity for abstract classes with amalgamation*,
  Ann. Pure Appl. Logic 98 (1999), [arXiv:math/9809197](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/9809197)
- W. Boney, *Tameness from large cardinal axioms*, J. Symb. Log. 79 (2014),
  [arXiv:1303.0550](https://arxiv.org/abs/1303.0550)

An abstract elementary class (AEC) is a class `K` of structures in a fixed first-order language
`L` together with a partial order `≺_K` on `K` that behaves like elementary substructure.
Set-theoretically, `M ≺_K N` requires `M` to be a substructure of `N`. Since types in Lean are
not literally subsets of one another, we follow the standard equivalent presentation of an AEC
through its `K`-embeddings: an `L`-embedding `f : M ↪[L] N` is a `K`-embedding when `M, N ∈ K`
and the image `f(M)` satisfies `f(M) ≺_K N`. Unions of `≺_K`-chains become direct limits along
chains of `K`-embeddings.
-/

namespace ShelahsEventualCategoricityConjecture

open FirstOrder FirstOrder.Language Cardinal

universe u

/-- A class of `L`-structures together with a distinguished class of `L`-embeddings, the
`K`-embeddings. This is the raw data of an abstract elementary class. -/
structure AbstractClass (L : FirstOrder.Language.{u, u}) where
  /-- Membership in the class `K`. -/
  Mem (M : Type u) [L.Structure M] : Prop
  /-- `IsStrongEmb f` says that `f : M ↪[L] N` is a `K`-embedding, i.e. `f(M) ≺_K N`. -/
  IsStrongEmb {M N : Type u} [L.Structure M] [L.Structure N] (f : M ↪[L] N) : Prop

namespace AbstractClass

variable {L : FirstOrder.Language.{u, u}} (K : AbstractClass L)

/-- `K.IsLSNumber μ` says that `μ ≥ |L| + ℵ₀` and that for every `M ∈ K` and every subset `A` of
`M` there is `N ≺_K M` with `A ⊆ N` and `‖N‖ ≤ |A| + μ`. The Löwenheim–Skolem number of `K` is the
least such `μ`. -/
def IsLSNumber (μ : Cardinal.{u}) : Prop :=
  L.card + ℵ₀ ≤ μ ∧
    ∀ (M : Type u) [L.Structure M], K.Mem M → ∀ A : Set M,
      ∃ (N : Type u) (_ : L.Structure N) (f : N ↪[L] M),
        K.IsStrongEmb f ∧ A ⊆ Set.range f ∧ #N ≤ #A + μ

/-- The Löwenheim–Skolem number `LS(K)` of `K`: the least cardinal `μ ≥ |L| + ℵ₀` such that every
subset `A` of a model `M ∈ K` is contained in some `N ≺_K M` with `‖N‖ ≤ |A| + μ`. -/
noncomputable def lsNumber : Cardinal.{u} :=
  sInf {μ | K.IsLSNumber μ}

end AbstractClass

/-- An abstract elementary class (AEC) in the language `L`, presented through its
`K`-embeddings (see the module docstring). The axioms are those of Shelah (Definition 0.A of
arXiv:math/9809197) and Boney (Section 2 of arXiv:1303.0550):

* `≺_K` is a partial order on `K` (`isStrongEmb_refl`, `isStrongEmb_comp`);
* `K` and `≺_K` are closed under isomorphisms (`mem_of_equiv`, `isStrongEmb_equiv_comp`);
* coherence (`isStrongEmb_of_comp`);
* the Tarski–Vaught chain axioms (`mem_directLimit`, `isStrongEmb_directLimit_of`,
  `isStrongEmb_directLimit_lift`), stated for chains indexed by a nonempty well-order;
* the Löwenheim–Skolem axiom (`exists_isLSNumber`).

`M ≺_K N` in the set-theoretic sense corresponds to the inclusion `M ↪[L] N` being a
`K`-embedding. -/
structure AEC (L : FirstOrder.Language.{u, u}) extends AbstractClass L where
  /-- `K`-embeddings only relate members of `K`. -/
  mem_of_isStrongEmb {M N : Type u} [L.Structure M] [L.Structure N] {f : M ↪[L] N} :
    IsStrongEmb f → Mem M ∧ Mem N
  /-- `M ≺_K M` for `M ∈ K`. -/
  isStrongEmb_refl {M : Type u} [L.Structure M] : Mem M → IsStrongEmb (Embedding.refl L M)
  /-- `≺_K` is transitive: `K`-embeddings compose. -/
  isStrongEmb_comp {M N P : Type u} [L.Structure M] [L.Structure N] [L.Structure P]
    {f : M ↪[L] N} {g : N ↪[L] P} : IsStrongEmb f → IsStrongEmb g → IsStrongEmb (g.comp f)
  /-- `K` is closed under isomorphisms. -/
  mem_of_equiv {M N : Type u} [L.Structure M] [L.Structure N] : Mem M → (M ≃[L] N) → Mem N
  /-- `≺_K` is closed under isomorphisms: if `f(M) ≺_K N` and `e : N ≅ N'`, then
  `e(f(M)) ≺_K N'`. -/
  isStrongEmb_equiv_comp {M N N' : Type u} [L.Structure M] [L.Structure N] [L.Structure N']
    {f : M ↪[L] N} (e : N ≃[L] N') : IsStrongEmb f → IsStrongEmb (e.toEmbedding.comp f)
  /-- Coherence: if `M₀ ⊆ M₁` (via the `L`-embedding `g`), `M₁ ≺_K M₂` and `M₀ ≺_K M₂`, then
  `M₀ ≺_K M₁`. -/
  isStrongEmb_of_comp {M₀ M₁ M₂ : Type u} [L.Structure M₀] [L.Structure M₁] [L.Structure M₂]
    {g : M₀ ↪[L] M₁} {e : M₁ ↪[L] M₂} : IsStrongEmb e → IsStrongEmb (e.comp g) → IsStrongEmb g
  /-- Tarski–Vaught: the union of a `≺_K`-chain is in `K`. -/
  mem_directLimit {ι : Type u} [LinearOrder ι] [WellFoundedLT ι] [Nonempty ι]
    (G : ι → Type u) [∀ i, L.Structure (G i)] (f : ∀ i j, i ≤ j → G i ↪[L] G j)
    [DirectedSystem G fun i j h => f i j h] :
    (∀ i j h, IsStrongEmb (f i j h)) → Mem (Language.DirectLimit G f)
  /-- Tarski–Vaught: each member of a `≺_K`-chain is `≺_K` the union of the chain. -/
  isStrongEmb_directLimit_of {ι : Type u} [LinearOrder ι] [WellFoundedLT ι] [Nonempty ι]
    (G : ι → Type u) [∀ i, L.Structure (G i)] (f : ∀ i j, i ≤ j → G i ↪[L] G j)
    [DirectedSystem G fun i j h => f i j h] :
    (∀ i j h, IsStrongEmb (f i j h)) → ∀ i, IsStrongEmb (Language.DirectLimit.of L ι G f i)
  /-- Tarski–Vaught: if every member of a `≺_K`-chain is `≺_K N`, then so is the union of the
  chain. -/
  isStrongEmb_directLimit_lift {ι : Type u} [LinearOrder ι] [WellFoundedLT ι] [Nonempty ι]
    (G : ι → Type u) [∀ i, L.Structure (G i)] (f : ∀ i j, i ≤ j → G i ↪[L] G j)
    [DirectedSystem G fun i j h => f i j h] {N : Type u} [L.Structure N]
    (g : ∀ i, G i ↪[L] N) (Hg : ∀ i j hij x, g j (f i j hij x) = g i x) :
    (∀ i j h, IsStrongEmb (f i j h)) → (∀ i, IsStrongEmb (g i)) →
      IsStrongEmb (Language.DirectLimit.lift L ι G f g Hg)
  /-- Löwenheim–Skolem axiom: some cardinal `μ ≥ |L| + ℵ₀` is a Löwenheim–Skolem number. -/
  exists_isLSNumber : ∃ μ : Cardinal.{u}, toAbstractClass.IsLSNumber μ

namespace AEC

variable {L : FirstOrder.Language.{u, u}} (K : AEC L)

/-- `K` is categorical in `κ` if `K` has exactly one model of cardinality `κ` up to
isomorphism. -/
def IsCategoricalIn (κ : Cardinal.{u}) : Prop :=
  (∃ (M : Type u) (_ : L.Structure M), K.Mem M ∧ #M = κ) ∧
    ∀ (M N : Type u) [L.Structure M] [L.Structure N],
      K.Mem M → K.Mem N → #M = κ → #N = κ → Nonempty (M ≃[L] N)

/-- The Löwenheim–Skolem number of an AEC is a Löwenheim–Skolem number. -/
@[category API, AMS 3]
theorem isLSNumber_lsNumber : K.IsLSNumber K.lsNumber :=
  csInf_mem K.exists_isLSNumber

/-- The Löwenheim–Skolem number of an AEC is at least `|L| + ℵ₀`. -/
@[category API, AMS 3]
theorem card_add_aleph0_le_lsNumber : L.card + ℵ₀ ≤ K.lsNumber :=
  K.isLSNumber_lsNumber.1

/-- The class of all `L`-structures, with every `L`-embedding as a `K`-embedding, is an AEC. -/
@[category test, AMS 3]
theorem exists_univ (L : FirstOrder.Language.{u, u}) :
    ∃ K : AEC L, (∀ (M : Type u) [L.Structure M], K.Mem M) ∧
      ∀ {M N : Type u} [L.Structure M] [L.Structure N] (f : M ↪[L] N), K.IsStrongEmb f := by
  refine ⟨{ Mem := fun _ _ => True
            IsStrongEmb := fun _ => True
            mem_of_isStrongEmb := fun _ => ⟨trivial, trivial⟩
            isStrongEmb_refl := fun _ => trivial
            isStrongEmb_comp := fun _ _ => trivial
            mem_of_equiv := fun _ _ => trivial
            isStrongEmb_equiv_comp := fun _ _ => trivial
            isStrongEmb_of_comp := fun _ _ => trivial
            mem_directLimit := by intros; trivial
            isStrongEmb_directLimit_of := by intros; trivial
            isStrongEmb_directLimit_lift := by intros; trivial
            exists_isLSNumber := ⟨L.card + ℵ₀, le_rfl, fun M _ _ A =>
              ⟨Substructure.closure L A, inferInstance, (Substructure.closure L A).subtype, trivial,
                ?_, ?_⟩⟩ },
    fun _ _ => trivial, fun _ => trivial⟩
  · rw [Substructure.coe_subtype, Subtype.range_coe]
    exact Substructure.subset_closure
  · have h := Substructure.lift_card_closure_le (L := L) (s := A)
    rw [lift_id, lift_id, lift_id] at h
    refine h.trans (max_le (le_trans le_add_self le_add_self) ?_)
    gcongr
    refine le_trans ?_ le_self_add
    unfold Language.card Language.Symbols
    rw [mk_sum, lift_id, lift_id]
    exact le_self_add

end AEC

/-- **Shelah's eventual categoricity conjecture.**
For every cardinal $\lambda$ there exists a cardinal $\mu(\lambda)$ such that if an AEC $K$ with
$\operatorname{LS}(K) \le \lambda$ is categorical in a cardinal $\kappa \ge \mu(\lambda)$
(i.e. $K$ has exactly one model of cardinality $\kappa$ up to isomorphism), then it is
categorical in all cardinals $\ge \mu(\lambda)$. -/
@[category research open, AMS 3]
theorem shelahs_eventual_categoricity_conjecture :
    ∀ lam : Cardinal.{u}, ∃ μ : Cardinal.{u}, ∀ (L : FirstOrder.Language.{u, u}) (K : AEC L),
      K.lsNumber ≤ lam → (∃ κ, μ ≤ κ ∧ K.IsCategoricalIn κ) →
        ∀ κ, μ ≤ κ → K.IsCategoricalIn κ := by
  sorry

end ShelahsEventualCategoricityConjecture

modeling_decisions: 'Above μ(λ)' is read as `μ ≤ κ` (non-strict), following Boney's statement (D.(3a)) and the Wikipedia article; this is equivalent to a strict reading up to adjusting μ.
The hypothesis is `LS(K) ≤ λ` exactly as in the list entry (not `= λ` as in Boney); equivalent by taking μ monotone.

AECs are presented through their class of `K`-embeddings (`IsStrongEmb`) instead of a literal substructure relation, because Lean types are not subsets of one another. `M ≺_K N` corresponds to the inclusion being a `K`-embedding; unions of chains are direct limits (`FirstOrder.Language.DirectLimit`). This is the standard equivalent presentation (e.g. Beke–Rosický, Lieberman–Rosický–Vasey); the translation of each axiom is documented in the field docstrings. Iso-closure of `≺_K` is stated as post-composition with an isomorphism; pre-composition follows from reflexivity + `mem_of_equiv`.

Chain axioms are stated for chains indexed by a nonempty well-ordered `ι : Type u` (i.e. ordinals in `Ordinal.{u}`), with a `DirectedSystem` of `K`-embeddings; continuity of the chain is not required (equivalent to the continuous/ordinal formulation given the other axioms). The empty chain is excluded to avoid the degenerate claim that an empty structure lies in `K`.

The language and all models live in one universe: `L : FirstOrder.Language.{u, u}` and models in `Type u`, cardinals in `Cardinal.{u}`. This avoids `Cardinal.lift` and captures every AEC in a fixed set-theoretic universe; the theorem is universe-polymorphic.

`LS(K)` is defined as `sInf` of the set of Löwenheim–Skolem numbers (in the Wikipedia/Boney form `‖N‖ ≤ |A| + μ` with `μ ≥ |L| + ℵ₀`); the set is nonempty by the AEC axiom, so `sInf` is the least element (API lemma `AEC.isLSNumber_lsNumber`). Shelah's variant `LS' + |τ|` gives the same value given the other axioms.

`IsCategoricalIn κ` requires both existence of a model of cardinality `κ` and uniqueness up to `L`-isomorphism ('one and only one model', Shelah Def. 1.1); Mathlib's `Cardinal.Categorical` was not reused because it lacks the existence clause and is only for theories.
Structures on empty types are admitted by Mathlib's `L.Structure`; this does not affect the conjecture, which only concerns categoricity at cardinals ≥ μ(λ) ≥ ℵ₀ and the LS number.

Two `@[category API]` lemmas and one `@[category test]` theorem (`AEC.exists_univ`: the class of all `L`-structures with all `L`-embeddings is an AEC, proved without `sorry`) are included as the basic API tests the repository asks for with bespoke definitions.

/-- An abstract elementary class (AEC) in the first-order language `L`.

isomorphisms, and satisfies coherence, the Tarski–Vaught chain axioms and the Löwenheim–Skolem

recorded through its `K`-embeddings: an embedding `f : M ↪[L] N` is *strong* (`IsStrong f`) when

become direct limits (`FirstOrder.Language.DirectLimit`). -/

  /-- `IsStrong f` means that `f : M ↪[L] N` is a `K`-embedding, i.e. `f(M) ≺_K N`. -/

  /-- `≺_K` is a relation on `K`. -/

  /-- `≺_K` is reflexive on `K`. -/
  isStrong_refl : ∀ {M : Bundled.{u} L.Structure}, M ∈ carrier → IsStrong (Embedding.refl L M)
  /-- `≺_K` is transitive. -/
  isStrong_comp : ∀ {M N P : Type u} [L.Structure M] [L.Structure N] [L.Structure P]

  /-- `K` is closed under isomorphisms. -/
  mem_of_equiv : ∀ {M N : Bundled.{u} L.Structure}, M ∈ carrier → (M ≃[L] N) → N ∈ carrier
  /-- `≺_K` is invariant under isomorphisms. -/
  isStrong_of_equiv : ∀ {M M' N N' : Type u} [L.Structure M] [L.Structure M'] [L.Structure N]

  /-- Coherence: if `M₀ ≺_K M₂`, `M₁ ≺_K M₂` and `M₀ ⊆ M₁`, then `M₀ ≺_K M₁`. -/

  nonempty ordinal is `≺_K N`, then so is the union of the chain. -/
  isStrong_directLimit_lift : ∀ {ι : Type u} [LinearOrder ι] [WellFoundedLT ι] [Nonempty ι]
    (M : ι → Type u) [∀ i, L.Structure (M i)] (f : ∀ i j, i ≤ j → M i ↪[L] M j)
    [DirectedSystem M fun i j h => f i j h] (N : Type u) [L.Structure N] (g : ∀ i, M i ↪[L] N)
    (Hg : ∀ i j hij x, g j (f i j hij x) = g i x),
    (∀ i j (hij : i ≤ j), IsStrong (f i j hij)) → (∀ i, IsStrong (g i)) →
      IsStrong (Language.DirectLimit.lift L ι M f g Hg)
  /-- Löwenheim–Skolem axiom: there is a cardinal `μ ≥ |L| + ℵ₀` such that every subset `A` of a
  model `M ∈ K` is contained in some `N ≺_K M` with `N ∈ K` and `‖N‖ ≤ |A| + μ`. -/
  exists_lowenheimSkolem : ∃ μ : Cardinal.{u}, L.card + ℵ₀ ≤ μ ∧
    ∀ M ∈ carrier, ∀ A : Set M, ∃ N ∈ carrier, ∃ f : N ↪[L] M,
      IsStrong f ∧ A ⊆ Set.range f ∧ #N ≤ #A + μ

namespace AEC

variable {L : FirstOrder.Language.{u, u}}

instance : Membership (Bundled.{u} L.Structure) (AEC L) := ⟨fun K M => M ∈ K.carrier⟩

/-- `μ` is a Löwenheim–Skolem bound for `K`: `μ ≥ |L| + ℵ₀`, and every subset `A` of a model
`M ∈ K` is contained in some `N ≺_K M` with `N ∈ K` and `‖N‖ ≤ |A| + μ`. -/
def IsLSBound (K : AEC L) (μ : Cardinal.{u}) : Prop :=
  L.card + ℵ₀ ≤ μ ∧ ∀ M ∈ K, ∀ A : Set M, ∃ N ∈ K, ∃ f : N ↪[L] M,
    K.IsStrong f ∧ A ⊆ Set.range f ∧ #N ≤ #A + μ

/-- The Löwenheim–Skolem number `LS(K)` of `K`: the least Löwenheim–Skolem bound for `K`. -/
noncomputable def lsNumber (K : AEC L) : Cardinal.{u} :=
  sInf {μ | K.IsLSBound μ}

@[category API, AMS 3]
theorem isLSBound_lsNumber (K : AEC L) : K.IsLSBound K.lsNumber :=
  csInf_mem K.exists_lowenheimSkolem

@[category API, AMS 3]
theorem lsNumber_le {K : AEC L} {μ : Cardinal.{u}} (hμ : K.IsLSBound μ) : K.lsNumber ≤ μ :=
  csInf_le' hμ

/-- `K` is categorical in `κ` if it has exactly one model of cardinality `κ` up to isomorphism:
there is a model of cardinality `κ` in `K`, and any two such models are isomorphic. -/
def IsCategoricalIn (K : AEC L) (κ : Cardinal.{u}) : Prop :=
  (∃ M ∈ K, #M = κ) ∧ ∀ M ∈ K, ∀ N ∈ K, #M = κ → #N = κ → Nonempty (M ≃[L] N)

/-- The class of all `L`-structures, in which every embedding is strong, is an AEC. -/
@[category test, AMS 3]
def univ (L : FirstOrder.Language.{u, u}) : AEC L where
  carrier := Set.univ
  IsStrong _ := True
  mem_of_isStrong _ _ := ⟨trivial, trivial⟩
  isStrong_refl _ := trivial
  isStrong_comp _ _ _ _ := trivial
  mem_of_equiv _ _ := trivial
  isStrong_of_equiv _ _ _ _ := trivial
  isStrong_of_comp_eq _ _ _ _ _ _ := trivial
  directLimit_mem := by intros; exact ⟨trivial, fun _ => trivial⟩
  isStrong_directLimit_lift := by intros; trivial
  exists_lowenheimSkolem := by
    refine ⟨L.card + ℵ₀, le_rfl, fun M _ A => ⟨Bundled.of (Substructure.closure L A), trivial,
      (Substructure.closure L A).subtype, trivial,
      fun a ha => ⟨⟨a, Substructure.subset_closure ha⟩, rfl⟩, ?_⟩⟩
    have h := Substructure.lift_card_closure_le (L := L) (s := A)
    rw [lift_id, lift_id, lift_id] at h
    refine h.trans (max_le (le_add_self.trans le_add_self) (add_le_add_right ?_ _))
    exact (mk_le_of_injective Sum.inl_injective).trans le_self_add

end AEC

/-- **Shelah's eventual categoricity conjecture.**
For every cardinal $\lambda$ there exists a cardinal $\mu(\lambda)$ such that if an AEC $K$ with
$\operatorname{LS}(K) \le \lambda$ is categorical in some cardinal $\kappa \ge \mu(\lambda)$
(i.e. $K$ has exactly one model of cardinality $\kappa$ up to isomorphism), then $K$ is
categorical in every cardinal $\kappa \ge \mu(\lambda)$.

The bound $\mu(\lambda)$ depends only on $\lambda$, not on $K$ or on its language. -/
@[category research open, AMS 3]
theorem shelahs_eventual_categoricity_conjecture :
    ∀ lam : Cardinal.{u}, ∃ μ : Cardinal.{u}, ∀ (L : FirstOrder.Language.{u, u}) (K : AEC L),
      K.lsNumber ≤ lam → (∃ κ ≥ μ, K.IsCategoricalIn κ) → ∀ κ ≥ μ, K.IsCategoricalIn κ := by
  sorry

end ShelahsEventualCategoricityConjecture
attempts.decomposition_objections: None. The single-slot decomposition with quantifier order ∀λ ∃μ ∀K, the ≥ reading of 'above', LS(K) ≤ λ, and 'exactly one model up to isomorphism' were all followed; the article's stronger conjectures (Hanf-number threshold, ℶ_{ω₁} for L_{ω₁,ω}) were excluded as the table prescribes.
modeling_decisions: 'Categorical in a cardinal above μ(λ)' and 'all cardinals above μ(λ)' are read as ≥ μ (following the decomposition note, Boney's statement of Shelah's D.(3a), and the Wikipedia article); with < the statement is equivalent after adjusting μ.
Hypothesis is LS(K) ≤ λ exactly as in the list entry (Boney uses LS(K) = λ; equivalent since μ may be taken monotone).

The AEC (K, ≺_K) is encoded through its K-embeddings rather than a literal 'M is a subset of N' relation, since in type theory one structure is not a subset of another: `IsStrong f` for `f : M ↪[L] N` means f(M) ≺_K N, and M ≺_K N means the inclusion is strong. Each classical axiom is translated: partial order → `isStrong_refl`/`isStrong_comp` (antisymmetry is vacuous in this form); 'M ≺_K N ⇒ M ⊆ N' → embeddings; isomorphism closure → `mem_of_equiv`/`isStrong_of_equiv`; coherence → `isStrong_of_comp_eq` (M₀ ⊆ M₁ inside M₂ becomes f = g ∘ h); the relation lives on K → `mem_of_isStrong`. The two formulations are mutually inverse translations (f is a K-embedding iff f(M) ≺_K N; Shelah's Def. 0.B), so the class of AECs is the same.

Unions of ≺_K-chains are Mathlib direct limits `FirstOrder.Language.DirectLimit` of a `DirectedSystem` of embeddings indexed by a nonempty well-ordered type ι : Type u (i.e. a nonempty ordinal; the empty chain is excluded, as is implicit in the sources, otherwise the empty structure would be forced into K). Compatibility of the maps (`DirectedSystem`, `Hg`) is automatic for set-theoretic inclusions and is required here. The first chain axiom also asserts M_i ≺_K ⋃_j M_j, as in Boney's and Shelah's definitions (the Wikipedia article's wording omits this clause).

Löwenheim–Skolem: `IsLSBound K μ` is the article's/Boney's formulation (μ ≥ |L| + ℵ₀ and every A ⊆ M ∈ K lies in some N ≺_K M, N ∈ K, ‖N‖ ≤ |A| + μ); `lsNumber K := sInf` of the bounds, which is the least bound since the AEC axiom `exists_lowenheimSkolem` guarantees a bound exists (API lemmas `isLSBound_lsNumber`, `lsNumber_le`). Shelah's variant of LS (only |A| ≤ μ, plus |τ|) is equivalent given the chain axioms.

Categoricity in κ requires existence and uniqueness: there is a model in K of cardinality κ and any two such are L-isomorphic (Wikipedia 'exactly one', Shelah Def. 1.1 'one and only one'). Mathlib's `Cardinal.Categorical` (for theories) only asserts uniqueness and was not reused.

Everything lives in one universe u: L : Language.{u,u}, models are `Bundled.{u} L.Structure`, and λ, μ, κ, LS(K), |L| are in Cardinal.{u}; Type u plays the role of the set-theoretic universe, so no `Cardinal.lift`s are needed. The theorem is universe-polymorphic.

K is a `Set (Bundled L.Structure)`, so it may be a proper class of structures and may contain empty structures or models of size < LS(K); neither affects the conjecture, which only concerns cardinals ≥ μ and allows μ to be increased.
The variable λ is named `lam` because `λ` is a reserved token in Lean 4.

A `@[category test]` construction `AEC.univ L` (all L-structures, all embeddings strong) is included to witness that the bespoke `AEC` structure is satisfiable, using Mathlib's `Substructure.lift_card_closure_le` for the Löwenheim–Skolem axiom.
